title: Conformal construction of constrained initial data

items.title: Vacuum conformal constraint data
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematical definition of compact vacuum, zero-cosmological-constant conformal initial data and its algebraic constraint residuals; no embedded development, existence theorem, or empirical claim is asserted.
items.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty smooth three-manifold without boundary that is
**compact**: for every family $(U_a)_{a\in A}$ of open subsets of $\Sigma$
with $\Sigma=\bigcup_{a\in A}U_a$, there is a finite subset $F\subseteq A$
such that $\Sigma=\bigcup_{a\in F}U_a$. In this item, “vacuum” means that the stress-energy tensor is zero and the
cosmological constant is fixed at $\Lambda=0$. Let $\widetilde h$ be a smooth
Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $\widetilde\sigma$ be a smooth symmetric
covariant two-tensor field, let $\tau\in\mathbb R$ be constant, and let
$\phi\in C^\infty(\Sigma,\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\phi(p)>0$ at every $p\in\Sigma$.
Use the positive scalar $\phi$ as a dimensionless conformal factor.

Write $\widetilde D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $\widetilde h$ and
$D$ for that of the metric $h$ defined below. On covariant tensor fields, these
symbols also denote their induced product connections, with the dual and
tensor-factor rules of the product-connection supplier in Definition references.
In a chart, $\widetilde h^{ij}$
denotes the inverse matrix to $\widetilde h_{ij}$. It is smooth because
$\det(\widetilde h_{ij})>0$ and the matrix inverse is the adjugate divided by
the determinant. For any smooth Riemannian metric $m$ on $\Sigma$, with
Levi-Civita connection $D^m$, define
$$R^m(X,Y)Z:=D^m_XD^m_YZ-D^m_YD^m_XZ-D^m_{[X,Y]}Z.$$
In a chart, $R[m]^a{}_{bij}$ denotes the components of
$R^m(\partial_i,\partial_j)\partial_b$. Define
$\operatorname{Ric}(m)_{ij}:=R[m]^k{}_{ikj}$ and
$R(m):=m^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}(m)_{ij}$. In particular,
$\widetilde R:=R(\widetilde h)$, with the same curvature sign convention.
Define the scalar Laplacian by
$$\widetilde\Delta f:=\widetilde h^{ij} (\partial_i\partial_j f-\widetilde\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k f),$$
where $\widetilde\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ are the Christoffel symbols of
$\widetilde D$, given by the Levi-Civita Christoffel formula
in Definition references.
The curvature sign is the one displayed above. All traces, norms, raising of
indices and contractions in this item use the metric indicated by the
subscript. In particular,
$$\operatorname{tr}_{\widetilde h}\widetilde\sigma:=\widetilde h^{ij}\widetilde\sigma_{ij},\qquad |\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2:=\widetilde h^{ik}\widetilde h^{j\ell}\widetilde\sigma_{ij}\widetilde\sigma_{k\ell},\qquad (\operatorname{div}_{\widetilde h}\widetilde\sigma)_j:=\widetilde h^{ik}\widetilde D_i\widetilde\sigma_{kj}.$$
The tensor $\widetilde\sigma$ is **transverse-traceless** (TT) with respect
to $\widetilde h$ when it is symmetric and both displayed trace and divergence
vanish. The input tensor in this definition is required to be TT.

Define
$$h:=\phi^4\widetilde h,\qquad K:=\phi^{-2}\widetilde\sigma+\frac{\tau}{3}h.$$
Because $\phi>0$, $h$ is a smooth Riemannian metric; because
$\widetilde\sigma$ and $h$ are symmetric, $K$ is a smooth symmetric tensor.
Here $h$ is the candidate induced Riemannian metric and $K$ is the candidate
second fundamental form, with the library convention
$K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X n,Y)$ when the data are induced by a spacelike hypersurface
with future unit normal $n$. The pair is **vacuum conformal constraint data**.
It is abstract data on $\Sigma$; no embedding into a spacetime is part of this
definition. For its embedded Lorentzian interpretation assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as in the supplied smooth tangent-bundle
convention; the algebraic tensor definitions themselves use no choice
principle. Define the $h$-trace, squared norm and divergence by
$$\operatorname{tr}_hK:=h^{ij}K_{ij},\qquad |K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell},\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)_j:=h^{ik}D_iK_{kj}.$$
With $R(h)$ computed using $h$, define the Hamiltonian and momentum residuals
$$\mathcal H(h,K):=R(h)+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2,\qquad \mathcal M_j(h,K):=h^{ik}D_iK_{kj}-D_j(\operatorname{tr}_hK).$$
The data satisfy the vacuum constraint equations when
$\mathcal H(h,K)=0$ and $\mathcal M(h,K)=0$. For an embedded hypersurface,
these are the normal and normal-tangential Einstein constraints in the
specified $K$ convention.

Tensoriality of curvature and basis-independent contraction make these scalar
curvatures independent of the chart.
For dimensional bookkeeping in the SI length convention, $[\tau]=\mathrm m^{-1}$,
$[R(h)]=[\widetilde R]=[|\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2]
=[\widetilde\Delta]=\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $[\phi]=1$. Thus all terms in the
scalar constraint equation have units $\mathrm m^{-2}$.

items.title: Conformal reduction of the vacuum constraint equations
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Conditional mathematical identity for smooth compact vacuum conformal data with zero cosmological constant; it proves constraint equivalence only and no existence or spacetime development theorem.
items.statement:
Let $(h,K)$ be the vacuum conformal constraint data of the definition. Then
$\operatorname{tr}_hK=\tau$ and the momentum residual vanishes:
$$\mathcal M_j(h,K)=0.$$
The Hamiltonian residual is
$$\mathcal H(h,K)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad -8\widetilde\Delta\phi+\widetilde R\,\phi-|\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2\phi^{-7} +\frac{2}{3}\tau^2\phi^5=0.$$
The displayed scalar equation is the **Lichnerowicz equation** for these
constant-mean-curvature (CMC) vacuum data. Here CMC means that the trace
$\operatorname{tr}_hK$ is spatially constant; its value is $\tau$.

references.title: É. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, Lecture Notes in Physics 846 (2012; author preprint arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1), §6.3.3, §§6.4.1–6.4.2, §§6.5.2–6.5.3, and §§8.2.2–8.2.4
references.locator: Full 220-page lecture-note PDF retrieved; complete relevant sections inspected. Equations (6.48)–(6.52), (6.79)–(6.83), (6.101)–(6.104) and (8.5)–(8.8) give the scalar-curvature, tracefree-curvature, momentum and Hamiltonian transformations.

references.title: R. Bartnik and J. Isenberg, The Constraint Equations, in The Einstein Equations and the Large Scale Behavior of Gravitational Fields (Birkhäuser, 2004), arXiv:gr-qc/0405092v1
references.locator: Full 34-page review chapter retrieved; the relevant §4.1 discussion and equations (47)–(56) were inspected for the conformal free-data split and constant-mean-curvature Lichnerowicz equation.

items.title: Exact positive constant solution of the CMC constraint equation
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Exact algebraic solution of the zero-cosmological-constant CMC vacuum constraint equation in the stated constant-coefficient case; it is not a universal solvability theorem.
items.statement:
Let the vacuum conformal data be as in the definition, so that
$\widetilde\sigma$ is TT with respect to $\widetilde h$. Suppose the
conformal metric has $\widetilde R=0$ and
$|\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2=A$ is a positive constant, with constant
$\tau\ne0$. Then the Lichnerowicz equation has exactly one positive constant
solution,
$$\phi_0=\left(\frac{3A}{2\tau^2}\right)^{1/12}.$$
With a fixed length unit, $[A]=[\tau^2]=\mathrm m^{-2}$, so $\phi_0$ is
dimensionless. Uniqueness is only among positive constant solutions; no
uniqueness claim is made for arbitrary positive functions.

references.title: É. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, Lecture Notes in Physics 846 (2012; author preprint arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1), §§8.2.2–8.2.4
references.locator: Full 220-page lecture-note PDF retrieved; complete relevant §§8.2.2–8.2.4 inspected, including equations (8.5)–(8.8) and the following constant-mean-curvature discussion.

references.title: R. Bartnik and J. Isenberg, The Constraint Equations, in The Einstein Equations and the Large Scale Behavior of Gravitational Fields (Birkhäuser, 2004), arXiv:gr-qc/0405092v1
references.locator: Full 34-page review chapter retrieved; the relevant §4.1 discussion and equations (47)–(56) were inspected for the vacuum CMC Lichnerowicz equation and the caution that general free data need not yield a solution.

items.title: Positive Fourier inverse for the linearized CMC constraint
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Fourier analysis of the linearized vacuum CMC constraint operator at the stated flat-torus solution; it proves a positive linear inverse and no nonlinear nearby-data existence theorem.
items.statement:
Let $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ with dimensionless coordinates
$x^i\pmod{2\pi}$ and flat conformal metric
$\widetilde h=L_*^2\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2$, where $L_*>0$ is a fixed reference
length. Suppose $\widetilde\sigma$ has constant squared norm $A>0$ and
$\tau\ne0$, and let $\phi_0$ be the positive constant solution in the preceding
proposition. Put
$$c:=7A\phi_0^{-8}+\frac{10}{3}\tau^2\phi_0^4>0.$$
The directional linearization of the Lichnerowicz scalar expression at
$\phi_0$ is
$$\mathcal A v=-8\widetilde\Delta v+cv.$$
It is strictly positive on nonzero smooth real $v$. For every integer $s\ge2$,
the same differential expression, interpreted using weak derivatives, defines
a bounded bijection
$\mathcal A:H^{s+2}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$. With
Fourier coefficients relative to the normalized torus measure, its inverse is
$$\widehat{\mathcal A^{-1}f}(k)= \frac{\widehat f(k)}{8L_*^{-2}|k|^2+c},\qquad k\in\mathbb Z^3,$$
and, for $N_s(f)^2:=\sum_k(1+|k|^2)^s|\widehat f(k)|^2$,
$$N_{s+2}(\mathcal A^{-1}f)\le \min\{8L_*^{-2},c\}^{-1}N_s(f).$$
The equivalent derivative Sobolev norms therefore give a bounded
$H^s\to H^{s+2}$ inverse. This linear result does not assert nonlinear
differentiability of the constraint map or nearby-data solvability.

references.locator: Full 220-page lecture-note PDF retrieved; complete relevant scalar-curvature and CMC Lichnerowicz sections inspected, including equations (6.52), (6.103), (8.5)–(8.8) and the §8.2.4 uniqueness discussion.

title: Conformal construction of constrained initial data — Examples

items.title: Flat-torus vacuum data from a constant TT tensor
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Exact mathematical example of compact flat-torus vacuum constraint data with nonzero transverse-traceless part; it makes no empirical claim or spacetime-development assertion.
items.statement:
Let $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ have dimensionless periodic coordinates $x^i$
and conformal metric $\widetilde h=L_*^2\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2$, where
$L_*>0$ is a length. Let $\widetilde\sigma$ have constant covariant
components $\widetilde\sigma_{11}=a_*$, $\widetilde\sigma_{22}=-a_*$ and all
other components zero, where $a_*>0$ is a length. Fix a nonzero constant
$\tau$ with units $\mathrm m^{-1}$. Then
$|\widetilde\sigma|_{\widetilde h}^2=A:=2a_*^2/L_*^4>0$ and
$\widetilde R=0$. The unique positive constant solution
$\phi_0=(3A/(2\tau^2))^{1/12}$ gives
$h=\phi_0^4\widetilde h$ and
$K=\phi_0^{-2}\widetilde\sigma+(\tau/3)h$, which satisfy the vacuum
constraint equations. The tracefree part of $K$ is nonzero.

references.title: É. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, Lecture Notes in Physics 846 (2012; author preprint arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1), §§8.2.2–8.2.4
references.locator: Full 220-page lecture-note PDF retrieved; complete relevant §§8.2.2–8.2.4 inspected, including the TT equation and CMC specialization. The flat-torus constants in this example are verified locally.

references.title: R. Bartnik and J. Isenberg, The Constraint Equations, in The Einstein Equations and the Large Scale Behavior of Gravitational Fields (Birkhäuser, 2004), arXiv:gr-qc/0405092v1
references.locator: Full 34-page review chapter retrieved; complete relevant §4.1 inspected, including equations (47)–(56). The displayed torus constants are checked directly.

items.title: A flat-torus zero mode defeats uniqueness and coercivity
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Exact mathematical boundary example for the vacuum conformal constraint equation on a flat torus; no observation, global development, or general uniqueness claim is made.
items.statement:
Let $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ with flat conformal metric
$\widetilde h=L_*^2\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, set $\widetilde\sigma=0$ and $\tau=0$,
and fix $\Lambda=0$. Every positive constant $\phi=d$ solves the
Lichnerowicz equation, so the same free data admit infinitely many positive
constant conformal factors. At each such $d$, the linearized scalar operator is
$\mathcal A_0v=-8\widetilde\Delta v$. Define coercivity here to mean that
$\int v\mathcal A_0v\,d\mu\ge c_0\|v\|_{H^1}^2$ for some $c_0>0$ and every
smooth real $v$, using the normalized torus measure and the Sobolev norm of
the Fourier supplier. The operator is not coercive.

references.title: É. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, Lecture Notes in Physics 846 (2012; author preprint arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1), §§8.2.2–8.2.4
references.locator: Full 220-page lecture-note PDF retrieved; complete relevant §§8.2.2–8.2.4 inspected, including the CMC Lichnerowicz equation. The torus zero-mode calculation in this example is verified locally.

references.title: R. Bartnik and J. Isenberg, The Constraint Equations, in The Einstein Equations and the Large Scale Behavior of Gravitational Fields (Birkhäuser, 2004), arXiv:gr-qc/0405092v1
references.locator: Full 34-page review chapter retrieved; complete relevant §4.1 inspected, including equations (47)–(56) and the warning that not all free data are solvable.
